![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14195873/assets/8689a80bf3fddc055072d11837cd5bf2a6b4e966d935816fa1e8b68454774d24.png)

We need to create a cylindrical tin with no lid using $64\pi \,{cm}^{2}$ of a metal sheet. What is the radius $r$ of the cylinder that has the largest volume?
question.worked_solution:
First, let $r$ be the radius and $h$ be the height of the cylinder.

We wish to maximize the volume

$$
V=\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

We know that the surface area is fixed at $64\pi \,{cm}^{2},$ so we also have the constraint equation

$$
2\pi rh+\pi {r}^{2}=64\pi .
$$

Now, by making $h$ the subject of the constraint equation, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi rh & =64\pi -\pi {r}^{2} \\ h & =\frac{64\pi -\pi {r}^{2}}{2\pi r} \\ h & =\frac{64-{r}^{2}}{2r}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the above into our expression for $V,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}V(r) & =\pi {r}^{2}\times \frac{64-{r}^{2}}{2r} \\ V(r) & =\frac{(64r-{r}^{3})\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to maximize $V,$ so we need to differentiate $V$ and set the derivative equal to zero. The derivative is 

$$
{V}^{′}(r)=\frac{(64-3{r}^{2})\pi }{2}.
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives a stationary point, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(r) & =0 \\ \frac{(64-3{r}^{2})\pi }{2} & =0 \\ 64 & =3{r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{64}{3} \\ r & =\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{3}\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that, in the last step, we only considered the positive root because the radius $r$ must be positive.

Finally, we confirm that $r=\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{3}$ is a maximum using the second derivative test. The second derivative ${V}^{″}(r)$ is

$$
{V}^{″}(r)=\frac{-6\pi r}{2}=-3\pi r,
$$

and we can see that ${V}^{″}(\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{3})<0.$ So, the stationary point $r=\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{3}$ is indeed a maximum of $V(r).$

Therefore, the cylinder with the largest volume has a radius of $r=\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{3}\,\text{cm}.$
